mem.10:
Jolene and Deborah’s conversation (Jan–Mar 2023)

- Jan 16–22, 2023: Jolene finished a demanding electrical engineering project. Deborah visited her late mother’s old house, full of memories; her mother had died a few years earlier. Her mother loved sitting on a special window-side bench each morning to enjoy the view. Deborah sometimes sits there to feel connected to her. Jolene’s mother died in 2022; Jolene remembers her room, which had a bench and window. In Paris in 2010, Jolene’s mother gave her a heart-shaped pendant depicting a bird; Jolene sees it as a symbol of freedom and a reminder to pursue goals. Deborah also has a pendant/keepsake connected to her mother.
- Deborah teaches yoga, hoping to help people find peace and joy. Yoga helped her through a difficult period. She visits her mother’s former home to do yoga and sit by the window, where she feels her mother’s presence and finds peace. Her mother read and smiled at a favorite spot each night; reading and travel were among her passions.
- Jan 25, 2023: Deborah’s father died suddenly. On Jan 27 she told Jolene the family was shell-shocked. She coped by spending time with family, cherishing memories, and living fully. Looking through family photos brought peace; her parents married in 1993. Deborah and her husband try to be as good a family as her parents were; love, openness, and mutual support keep them close and happy. On Jan 26, members of Deborah’s group sent a letter thanking her for her positive influence; it reminded her why she loves yoga.
- Jolene has snakes Susie and Seraphim, which calm and cheer her. Seraphim once escaped and curled beside her while she gamed. Jolene and her partner both love gaming; they played Detroit on console during Jan 20–26 and planned The Walking Dead for Jan 28. Jolene learned gaming independently as a child. On Feb 1 they planned another console game.
- Feb 1: Jolene’s engineering professor assigned a large robotics project. She felt excited and nervous but enjoyed designing/programming it as a puzzle. That day she also took a mini-retreat, gained a new outlook and confidence after realizing she had achieved more than expected, and found solutions for her project.
- By Feb 4, Jolene had recently felt on an emotional rollercoaster but was coping. The prior week she planned, researched, designed, and built a sustainable water purifier for a rural community. It was challenging and rewarding; seeing it supply clean water felt surreal and purposeful, showing engineering can improve lives. She wants an engineering career creating sustainable solutions for underserved communities. She is interested in green technology and helping disadvantaged areas.
- Jolene proposed volunteering to teach STEM to underprivileged children, potentially through local schools/centers and workshops with engineer guest speakers. On Feb 9 she had not contacted organizations yet, wanting to solidify the plan. She shared a planner photo with notebook, pen, and notes.
- Deborah met neighbor Anna at park yoga on Jan 31; they discussed yoga’s benefits and community. On Feb 3 they took a class together, tried dance poses including Warrior II; Deborah said it builds strength/focus and that mutual support brought them closer. Deborah described a chair twist: sit at chair edge, feet planted, twist and support a hand on knee, hold a few breaths, switch; stretches back/shoulders and relaxes muscles. Anna wears a pendant for her mother; sharing mother-related keepsakes brought her and Deborah closer.
- Jolene likes Sapiens (human history and technology) and read Neal Stephenson’s Avalanche in one sitting around Jan 21. A story about someone overcoming many challenges reinforced her belief that hard work and belief make anything possible.
- A friend gave Deborah flowers during a struggle; the bouquet brings hope, courage, warmth, appreciation. Forest trails and a nearby beach are favorite nature spots; forest calms her, and waves/sand bring peace and happiness. Deborah visits water near her mother’s former home to reflect, bringing her mother’s amulet; holding it makes her feel loved and comforted. She enjoys birdsong and breezes. Jolene’s summer 2022 Bogotá vacation photo showed a beach sunset; she found it beautiful, calming, and a reminder of nature’s power.
- Feb 21: Jolene had dinner and drinks with friends and enjoyed letting her hair down. Feb 22: Deborah visited a flower garden, finding it calming and nostalgic; roses and dahlias bring her peace. A friend had died the prior week; remembering their time together helped her through grief and reminded her life is special. A photo with Karlie from a hike the previous summer was their last together; seeing it made Deborah smile. Deborah visited Bali in 2022 and loved its peaceful beauty for yoga; waves and fresh air made beach yoga wonderful. Jolene said she wanted to try beach yoga.
- Feb 25: Jolene was balancing engineering school, her partner’s video games, yoga and meditation. Yoga helps her relax, gain perspective, feel alert and motivated. She and her partner had been together three years, were unmarried and taking things slowly; a ring in a photo was decorative, not a wedding ring. They met in a college engineering class, became friends then partners, enjoy engineering projects together, and understand each other’s work struggles. Partner sometimes joins yoga, helping them bond. When overwhelmed, Jolene breathes or meditates for calm and clarity. Deborah meditates, does yoga and teaches mornings, spends evenings with loved ones; exercise connects her to her body. She jogged in a nearby park for the first time Feb 24 and planned to make it routine. Feb 25 photo of a person on a bench at sunset reminded her to find peace amid chaos.
- Mar 2: Anna had recently brought Deborah vegan tofu-and-vegetable stir-fry with ginger and soy sauce. Jolene likes lasagna and was busy with studies/exams. On Feb 24 Jolene did yoga/meditation for self-care; Deborah also did both to reset. Feb 26 Jolene took Seraphim to a park; the snake enjoyed exploring. People are surprised to see a tamed snake; accompanying photo actually showed a lizard among leaves.
- Mar 2 Jolene wanted to monitor stress and mental health, but studies made her neglect self-care; exams/deadlines overwhelmed her and her to-do list seemed endless. Deborah advised breaking study into small goals, using a planner, and making time for herself; offered a study plan. Deborah promised a mug like a photo’s yellow cup with handwritten message; Jolene said it cheered her up.
- Mar 10 Deborah hosted a neighborhood yoga class; a photo showed women posing together. Neighbors enjoyed it. On Mar 13 Deborah said teaching began because yoga calmed her and she wanted to share that; helping people find peace/awareness makes her happy and builds friendships/community. She started a neighborhood class and enjoyed its positive impact.
- Mar 13 Jolene struggled with engineering assignments and asked to discuss time management. They agreed to find a time; Jolene would check her schedule and get back to Deborah; no time was set. Deborah offered support and suggested catching up.
- Mar 22 Deborah checked in about Jolene’s stressful exams/deadlines. Jolene used Pomodoro (25 minutes work, 5-minute break) but struggled to prioritize. Deborah uses daily schedules/to-do lists and shared a notepad photo. Jolene found her own large task lists overwhelming; she shared notes on a counter, an example from Mar 17. Deborah explained the four-quadrant Eisenhower Matrix (urgency/importance), with a photo of scissors on paper; Jolene found it helpful and planned to try it.
- Deborah and Anna had recently watched sunset by the sea and talked about inspiring each other. Asked what a beach photo of a person with surfboard evoked, Jolene said she wanted to learn surfing but lacked time. She had gathered information, watched videos, and obtained a beginner’s guide but still needed to find lesson time/place. Deborah encouraged
mem.20:
Jolene and Deborah are friends who support each other. Deborah teaches yoga/mindfulness; Jolene studies engineering. Dates are in 2023 unless stated otherwise.

Family, grief:
- Jolene’s mother died in 2022. In Paris in 2010 she gave Jolene a heart-shaped pendant with a bird, a symbol of freedom and pursuing goals. Jolene remembers her mother’s house, especially her room’s window and bench.
- Deborah’s mother died years before 2023. She loved travel, art, flowers, and quiet moments by a window on a special bench. Deborah sometimes sits or does yoga in the old house to feel close to her. Her parents married in 1993; Deborah and her husband value love, openness and mutual support, like her parents. Deborah wears her mother’s pendant/amulet; holding it by a waterside spot near the old house comforts her. Art shows feel like sharing the experience with her mother.
- Deborah’s father died suddenly on 2023-01-25. On Jan 27 she told Jolene the family was shell-shocked. Family time, memories, a photo album and living fully helped her cope. She lost friend Karlie shortly before 2023-02-22; their last photo together was from a hike the previous summer. Roses, dahlias and visiting a garden comforted her.
- On 2023-08-21 Deborah revisited a meaningful place and sat on the bench where she and her mother used to chat. She felt nostalgia, longing and gratitude, and brought flowers. Her mother loved flowers and simple pleasures; she taught Deborah to slow down, notice beauty and find joy. Deborah shared photos of flowers, a woman with red roses, and a waterside sunset.

Deborah:
- Yoga helped her through a hard period; she teaches to share calm, peace and joy. Values community, self-awareness, emotional wellbeing and personal growth; leads yoga, meditation and self-care workshops. Her group thanked her in a letter on 2023-01-26.
- Met neighbor Anna at park yoga on 2023-01-31; bonded through yoga and maternal keepsakes. Attended a Feb 3 class including Warrior II. Deborah explained supported seated twist: sit at chair edge, feet grounded, twist with hand on knee, breathe and switch sides; stretches back/shoulders and relaxes tense muscles. Started neighborhood yoga class by Mar 10; enjoyed its effects and friendships by Mar 13.
- Jogged in a nearby park for the first time Feb 24, planned regular morning runs; started running group with Anna in July. Organized a July yoga event with food stalls/live music, coordinating with nearby businesses/venues. Led yoga/meditation for care-home residents during week of Aug 7. Started community cleanup/fundraising by Aug 1. Made a meditation guide for retreat by Aug 12.
- Attended retreat with like-minded friends on June 26; tried Dancer and Tree poses. Retreat statue symbolized peace/enlightenment; shared a lake sunset photo. Enjoys a park with forest trail, beach and a bench where she and her mother discussed dreams/life and once watched a sunset in silence. Nature, waves, sand, birds and breeze restore her; visits waterside near mother’s old home. Visited Bali in 2022 and loved beach yoga, waves and fresh air. Biked with a neighbor and visited an art show with a friend in week before Apr 9.
- Yoga, meditation, walks and mindful attention ground her; walks can feel like a “reboot.” Likes mellow instrumental music, including “Savana,” and recommends the album “Sleep.” Bought yoga props, a candle and essential oils. Used to play detective games with her husband, taking turns; hadn’t played recently by Aug 19.

Jolene:
- Engineering student; wants engineering to benefit disadvantaged communities. Completed a hard electrical-engineering project around Jan 16–22. In early Feb designed/built a sustainable water purifier for a rural community; it worked, bringing purpose and deep satisfaction. Feb 1 had a large robotics assignment: exciting but nerve-racking, enjoyed design/programming as a puzzle; mini-retreat gave perspective, confidence and solutions. Proposed volunteer STEM workshops for underprivileged children with schools/centers and guest engineers; hadn’t contacted them by Feb 9, wanting a stronger plan. Shared planner sketches Feb 9; project breakthrough Mar 24.
- Finished challenging solar-powered vehicle project in May (photo June 6), proud of perseverance. By June she interned at a well-known engineering firm, applying school knowledge to real projects; photo showed construction-worker colleagues. Internship strengthened her interest but work-life balance was difficult. Did yoga atop Mount Talkeetna June 5.
- Has practiced yoga/meditation sporadically for about three years, essential for stress and centering. On June 26 felt hectic/overwhelmed but determined; reported breakthrough and shared house drawing. Major project crash Aug 1 destroyed all files after substantial work; frustrating/depressing. Meditation helped restore calm and clarity (Aug 12). Designed blue-covered notebooks with galaxies/circuitry, inspired by space and engines; art/design gave fresh problem-solving perspectives. By Aug 12 prototyping affordable, productive aerial surveillance for emergency response, environmental monitoring and safety. Aug 16 struggled to balance engineering, relationship and personal growth; started bullet journaling/time management and enjoyed crossing off tasks; quote reminded her not to give up. Studies going well; balance matters.
- Snakes Susie (adopted around Aug 2021 when lonely; species unspecified) and Seraphim (female, acquired 2022) calm and cheer her. Seraphim escaped once and curled beside her while gaming; another time found under bed after hours’ search. Jolene took Seraphim to park Feb 26; related photo showed a lizard among leaves. Bought aquarium June 24; shared Seraphim photos June 26. Snake care helps her slow down and tune into herself.
- Jolene and her male partner met in college engineering class, became friends then a couple; together three years by Feb 25, unmarried and taking it slowly. Share engineering projects, yoga and gaming; yoga together bonds them. Played Detroit in January, planned The Walking Dead Jan 28; enjoy It Takes Two and Overcooked 2. Jolene once won three large pizzas in Overcooked 2 bets. Bought him a console gift Aug 17 (black Xbox by Yoda); he played it. They game to relax and bond.
- Jolene learned gaming as a child. On Aug 21 said they received Battlefield 1 for the console the previous week.
- Reads; liked Sapiens and read Neal Stephenson’s “Avalanche” in one sitting around Jan 21; inspired by a story of success through challenges. Favorite dish: lasagna.
- Exams/deadlines overwhelmed her Mar 2. Deborah advised smaller blocks, goals and planner, offered help. Jolene used Pomodoro (25 minutes work/5 break), struggled to prioritize; Deborah introduced Eisenhower Matrix and shared task-notepad photo; Jolene planned to try it. Mar 17 notepad photo showed large overwhelming task list. Uses breathing/meditation breaks, yoga and self-care; yoga improves relaxation, perspective, alertness and motivation. Deborah recommended mindful breathing June 6 and offered mindfulness help Aug 16; Jolene was interested.
- Likes Nils Frahm and Ólafur Arnalds for yoga; lavender/rosemary scents and candles.
- On Aug 21 said she was trying to do more yoga and meditation to relax/focus and was “finding my zen again.” Favorite restful pose is savasana/corpse pose; finds it calming and a way to let go. Had done yoga for three years, using it to escape study/work stress. Shared a photo of a green cushion by a window and a funny image of someone lying on the floor with a paper bag.

Both value support, slowing down, mindfulness, nature and simple moments. Jolene likes beach sunsets; she took a Bogotá vacation (details not recorded).
mem.30:
People
- Deborah and Jolene are close friends who discuss family, grief, yoga, books, nature, and trying new activities. Jolene studies engineering; Deborah teaches yoga and organizes community activities.
- Deborah is married; she and her husband value love, openness, and mutual support. Jolene has a male partner she met in an engineering class; they were friends first and had been together three years by 2023-02-25. They share engineering, yoga, gaming, and travel interests.

Family, grief, keepsakes
- Jolene’s mother died in 2022. In 2010 she gave Jolene a heart-shaped pendant with a bird in Paris; its freedom symbolism encourages Jolene to pursue goals. Jolene remembers her mother’s room and window-side bench; her mother taught perseverance and helping others.
- Deborah’s parents married in 1993. Her father died suddenly on 2023-01-25; on 2023-01-27 she told Jolene the family was shell-shocked. Photos and time with family helped her grieve. Her mother loved travel, books, flowers, and reading by a window at night. Deborah visits her mother’s old home and sits on a meaningful bench; she wears a keepsake of her mother. Her mother loved cooking and bringing family together; Deborah especially loved her mother’s pineapple birthday cakes as a child.
- Deborah’s friend Karlie died shortly before 2023-02-22. A hiking photo from the previous summer was their last time together. Roses and dahlias comfort Deborah. In September 2023 Deborah reconnected with her mother’s old friends, sharing memories and photos.
- Deborah’s yoga group sent her a grateful letter on 2023-01-26.

Jolene
- Aspires to engineer sustainable solutions for communities; interested in clean water, renewables, green technology, and social good. Completed a rural-community water purifier shortly before 2023-02-04; did robotics on 2023-02-01; completed a solar vehicle in May 2023; built an affordable aerial emergency/environmental-monitoring prototype by 2023-08-12. Lost project files in a July 2023 crash but persisted. Engineering-firm internship in June 2023 challenged her work-life balance. Considered volunteering to teach STEM to underserved children but had not contacted schools by 2023-02-09.
- She and her partner visited Rio de Janeiro in August 2023 and attended a Phuket retreat in September. On 2023-08-17 she bought him an Xbox (photo also showed a Yoda figure); his father taught him determination.
- Gaming: began at age 10 when parents gave her a console; father supported her and mother played too. Favorite game with mother was Monster Hunter: World. Plays Detroit, It Takes Two, and Overcooked 2 with partner; once won three pizzas betting. Recommends Zelda: Breath of the Wild, Animal Crossing: New Horizons, Overcooked 2. Gaming helps her decompress and connect.
- Pet snakes: Susie (female, adopted around August 2021; calming companion) and Seraphim (female, acquired 2022; escaped once and was found under bed, once curled beside Jolene while she gamed). Number of snakes otherwise unclear. Jolene took Seraphim to a park in February 2023 and bought an aquarium in June. Snake care connects her to nature and teaches patience.
- Has practiced yoga/meditation for about three years by June 2023; helps with stress, focus, motivation, perspective. Likes savasana, candles, lavender/rosemary oils, soft music (Nils Frahm, Ólafur Arnalds); meditates near a pond. Uses breaks, breathing, Pomodoro, planners/bullet journal, Eisenhower Matrix. Exams stressful in March and September. Phuket retreat reflection: release expectations and appreciate the present.
- Reads Neal Stephenson’s “Avalanche” (read in one sitting around 2023-01-21) and likes “Sapiens.” Likes lasagna. Shared planner sketches on 2023-02-09. Used to bake chocolate-chip cookies with someone close; ideal cookies are warm, gooey chocolate and soft, buttery.
- On 2023-09-15, she and partner tried a scuba lesson, enjoyed it, found a dive spot, and she considered certification. Deborah is interested in underwater life but has not scuba-dived.
- Jolene has not surfed previously; began learning surfing and invited Deborah to try. They planned to find a suitable time, likely October 2023; Jolene would check her schedule. Jolene also suggested visiting her peaceful lake and watching a sunrise (2023-09-06).
- On 2023-09-20, Jolene said she and her partner had just returned from a peaceful yoga retreat (place unspecified); sunrise colors during yoga made them feel alive, grateful, peaceful, and connected to nature and themselves. Shared a photo of sunset over a valley with a horse. Recalled a peaceful waterfall oasis found hiking with her partner, where worries vanished; planned another nature outing in October. Shared photo of a plant growing from a building corner as a symbol of growth through obstacles and hope in tough times.

Deborah
- Teaches yoga for peace, balance, and community; yoga helped her through a difficult period. Practices at her mother’s old home; nearby waterside spot and park sunset bench are comforting memorial places.
- Met neighbor Anna at park yoga on 2023-01-31; bonded in class (including Warrior II) by 2023-02-03. Deborah taught a modified chair twist for back/shoulders. Hosted neighborhood yoga on 2023-03-10; organized July event with yoga, food stalls, live music, local businesses. Runs with Anna; started a running group on 2023-07-09. Leads mindfulness/self-care workshops; led yoga-meditation for seniors during week of 2023-08-07. Yoga friends feel like family; she and Anna share mother-memorial pendants.
- On 2023-09-16 Deborah and a neighbor held a free community gardening class for all ages. She enjoyed sharing plant knowledge and helping people care for the world.
- Enjoys nature, yoga, meditation, jogging, biking, beach/forest walks and reflection. Cats Luna (shelter adoption, age 5 on 2023-08-26) and Max (late mother’s cat, age 8); dislikes dogs. Visited Bali in 2022; likes beach yoga. Storm cancelled a yoga getaway on 2023-09-08. August 2023 retreat near mother’s home felt life-changing. Favorite yoga music: “Savana” and album “Sleep.” Has surfed; discovered surfing at a beach special to her.
- Anna brought Deborah vegan tofu-vegetable stir-fry. On 2023-03-02 Deborah gave Jolene a yellow mug with handwritten message.
- On 2023-09-10 Deborah visited her mother’s old home and sat on the bench, feeling her mother’s loving presence. Shared photos of a food bowl and a pineapple cake with a smiley face.
- Deborah enjoys reading as an escape; showed Jolene her living-room bookshelf. Shared cozy nook/bathroom-stool photo and beach-surfer photo. Jolene said her bathroom has an aesthetic vibe and a self-discovery book she read there resonated with her; shared photo of someone reading on a bed.
- On 2023-09-20 Deborah said she had enjoyed a music festival with friends: dancing felt freeing, music brought people together and expressed feelings. It reminded her of her mother’s soothing lullabies. Shared memory of a pink blossom tree near home blooming each spring; it felt like nature’s artwork, inspired awe and appreciation of life, and symbolized hope for growth. Jolene shared the resilient plant photo; both discussed holding onto small positive things during hard times.

Plans and shared activities
- On 2023-09-15 Deborah and Jolene planned coffee at 5 p.m.; Jolene was sorting books, Deborah would bring interesting books and later mention a hidden coffee shop. They also planned to play Deborah’s unnamed cat-themed attack-card game.
- On 2023-09-17 they discussed trying surfing together, likely October; Deborah eagerly agreed.
- On 2023-09-20 Jolene said it was great catching up and encouraged Deborah to keep finding beauties in life.
